pattern.deadline_window: Full-paper deadline Sep 24 - Oct 1 (2024: Sep 28; 2025: Oct 1; 2026: Sep 24; 2027: Sep 25), 11:59pm AoE. Mandatory abstract deadline 4-7 days earlier (Sep 18 - Sep 27; 2024's was extended Sep 21 -> Sep 23). No paper-deadline extension in any of the last four cycles.
pattern.typical_notification_month: January for 2024-2026 (Jan 15 / Jan 22 / Jan 25); moved to mid-December for 2027 (Dec 16, 2026) - roughly 12 weeks after the deadline.
pattern.typical_conference_month: Late April to early May (2024: May 7-11; 2025: Apr 24-28; 2026: Apr 23-27; 2027: Apr 26-30); 3 main-conference days followed by 2 workshop days.
pattern.location_rotation: Rotates across continents: Vienna, Europe (2024) -> Singapore, Asia (2025) -> Rio de Janeiro, South America (2026) -> San Francisco, North America (2027); Kigali, Africa in 2023.
pattern.review_process: Double-blind, fully public reviewing on OpenReview: reviews, author responses and the author-reviewer discussion are posted publicly (author names revealed only after decisions), followed by a private reviewer/AC discussion and meta-review. Withdrawn submissions stay public and are de-anonymized. Reciprocal reviewing has been required since ICLR 2025: authors on 3+ papers must review at least 6, and every submission needs a registered qualified reviewer-author.

resubmission_rules.dual_submission: Submissions that are identical (or substantially similar) to versions that have been previously published, or accepted for publication, or that have been submitted in parallel to this or other conferences or journals, are not allowed and violate our dual submission policy.
resubmission_rules.arxiv: Allowed: 'papers that have appeared on non-peer reviewed websites (like arXiv) or that have been presented at workshops (i.e., venues that do not have publication proceedings) do not violate the policy.' Cite your own preprints in the third person to preserve anonymity.
resubmission_rules.neurips_resubmission: No formal NeurIPS->ICLR rule; the norm is that NeurIPS rejects (NeurIPS notifications land within days of the ICLR deadline - Sep 24, 2026 vs ICLR 2027 paper deadline Sep 25, 2026) get revised and resubmitted to ICLR. Because the ICLR abstract deadline is mandatory and falls a week before the paper deadline, the abstract must be registered before the NeurIPS decision arrives; the paper must not be under review at both venues simultaneously (withdraw from the other venue first).
resubmission_rules.submission_caps_2027: Max 20 submissions per author; at most one submission per author on which no co-author is an eligible reciprocal reviewer (first-time authors effectively limited to one paper).
resubmission_rules.rejected_papers: Rejected ICLR papers may be resubmitted elsewhere; reviews remain public on OpenReview. Withdrawn papers remain publicly visible and de-anonymized.
resubmission_rules.page_limit: 9 pages main text at submission (10 for rebuttal/camera-ready), references and appendix excluded.
resubmission_rules.deadline_firmness: Official wording: 'the deadlines are final and we cannot make any accommodations for missing the abstract deadline or paper deadline.'

notes: AS OF 2026-09-21 THE ABSTRACT DEADLINE (Sep 18, 2026 11:59 PM AoE) HAS PASSED and the paper deadline is Fri Sep 25, 2026 11:59 PM AoE (= Sat Sep 26 11:59 UTC). Earlier than the 'late Sept / early Oct' pattern by ~1 week.

The abstract deadline is mandatory and hard: 'the deadlines are final and we cannot make any accommodations for missing the abstract deadline or paper deadline.' No extension announced on the CFP, Dates, Author Guidelines, blog, or secondary trackers as of today.
Between abstract and paper deadline: titles and abstracts may be edited; author order may change but authors cannot be added/removed; no edits at all after the paper deadline.

Timeline is compressed vs 2026: reviews Nov 5; author-reviewer discussion Nov 5-18 (2 weeks, vs 3 weeks in 2026); reviewer-AC discussion/meta-reviewing Nov 19-Dec 16; final decisions Dec 16, 2026 (about 5-6 weeks earlier than the January decisions of 2024-2026).

New 2027 submission caps (blog, Sep 2 2026): no author on more than 20 submissions; each author on at most one paper in which no author is an eligible reciprocal reviewer ('new authors' = never published at a major AI/ML/CV/robotics/NLP conference). Authors on 3+ papers must review at least 6 papers; every paper needs a registered qualified reviewer-author.
Page limit: 9 pages main text at submission, 10 for rebuttal/camera-ready; references/appendix excluded.

Location: the 2027 landing page says only 'California' with 'Venue information will be posted here'; 'San Francisco, California, US' is stated on the official Call for Workshops page and 'San Francisco, CA, USA' on the OpenReview venue group. Moscone Center appears only as an image caption on iclr.cc and in the ai-deadlines entry - treat the venue as likely but not formally announced.

Conference: main conference Apr 26-28, workshops Apr 29-30, 2027 (the Call for Workshops page has a typo 'April 29 and 30, 2026'). Workshop proposal deadline Oct 9, 2026 AoE; workshop notification Nov 29, 2026.

NeurIPS 2026 author notifications are Sep 24, 2026 AoE (neurips.cc Dates) - one day before the ICLR 2027 paper deadline and after the mandatory abstract deadline. A NeurIPS-rejected paper can only go to ICLR 2027 if its abstract was already registered by Sep 18; ICLR's dual-submission policy forbids parallel submission, so a paper still under review elsewhere at submission time is a violation.
Withdrawn ICLR papers remain publicly visible on OpenReview and are de-anonymized after the deadline (Author Guidelines).
Camera-ready deadline not yet announced (expected ~Feb-Mar 2027 by pattern: 2025 Mar 14, 2024 Apr 14, 2026 mid-Feb instructions).
